input.rationale: Resume the registered necessary gap (monotonic-store discriminator) whose prior run exited 1 in the harness helper's 5s shutdown timer. The harness now sets LongstopTimeout=60s and emits each scenario's CA_EVENT inside the scenario function, before the deferred cluster.Close runs, so a slow helper shutdown cannot hide a completed measurement. Scenarios, prefix, requirement and comparisons are unchanged from the predecessor.

scope.description: One process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with FileSnapshotStore; each scenario selects InmemStore directly (non-monotonic) or wrapped in MockMonotonicLogStore (monotonic) via MakeClusterCustom with LongstopTimeout=60s. The replacement leader compacts at or below its snapshot index (TrailingLogs=0).
assumptions: Config: ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, CommitTimeout=10ms, TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold disabled, SnapshotInterval=1h.
The isolated node's above-snapshot suffix is produced by real uncommitted Apply calls on the old leader before it steps down; no state is injected.
MockMonotonicLogStore returns IsMonotonic()==true, so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch.
excluded: Network and TCP transports; mixed-version rolling upgrades.
Restart or recovery of the isolated node; only live catch-up is measured.
Disk-backed stores.

experiment.prefix: For each of three scenarios: bootstrap a 3-node cluster, commit a 20-command prefix, isolate the current leader, append 2 (control) or 200 (both stall cases) uncommitted tail commands on the isolated node, let the remaining two nodes elect a replacement leader, commit 20 more commands and take a snapshot at index S, commit 10 post entries above S, reconnect, observe for about 4.5s, and emit the scenario's setup and result events before helper cleanup. The two stall scenarios differ only in the isolated node's log store (non-monotonic vs MockMonotonicLogStore).
experiment.requirement: After a follower installs a snapshot at index S, catch-up must not depend on whether the above-S bytes survive: regardless of the LogStore's monotonicity, a follower whose persisted log ended above S must stop reporting a last log entry above S and accept the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=S so it converges to the leader's log. Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries PrevLogEntry check); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 chooses removeOldLogs for a MonotonicLogStore and compactLogs otherwise, and is the producer responsible for the post-install last-log state.
experiment.responsibility: Follower snapshot installation establishing a post-install last-log state compatible with the leader's AppendEntries and nextIndex catch-up loop, for both monotonicity branches of the LogStore.

comparisons.description: Control: isolated log at or below the snapshot index reaches the leader commit index.
Non-monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix must catch up.
Monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix: removeOldLogs deletes the bytes, yet the cached last-log state must not block catch-up.

experiment.revision_reason: Harness-only change to fix the predecessor's independent cleanup failure: MakeClusterOpts.LongstopTimeout is raised from the helper default 5s to 60s, and each scenario's CA_EVENT pair is now printed inside the scenario function before the deferred cluster.Close. No scenario, app, source, requirement or comparison changed.

scope.description: One process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with InmemStore and FileSnapshotStore, built with the upstream MakeCluster test helper. The replacement leader compacts its log at or below its snapshot index (TrailingLogs=0) so it can no longer serve the isolated node's match point from the log store.
assumptions: Config: ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, CommitTimeout=10ms, TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold disabled, SnapshotInterval=1h.
The isolated node's uncommitted suffix is produced by real Apply calls on the old leader during its pre-step-down lease window; no state is injected.
The replacement leader commits post-snapshot entries with the third node so leader_commit_index rises above the snapshot index.
excluded: Network and TCP transports; mixed-version rolling upgrades.
Monotonic log stores; the non-monotonic InmemStore path is exercised.
Any restart or recovery of the isolated node; only live catch-up is measured.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap a 3-node cluster; commit a 20-command prefix to all nodes; isolate the current leader; append 200 (case) or 2 (control) uncommitted tail commands on the isolated node; let the remaining two nodes elect a replacement leader; commit 20 more commands and take a snapshot at index S on the replacement leader; commit 10 post entries above S; reconnect and observe for about 4.5s.
basis.requirement: After a follower installs a snapshot at index S and the follower's durable log ends at index L with S >= L, the follower must report its last log entry as (S, snapshotTerm) so the leader's PrevLogEntry=S consistency check succeeds and later entries commit on the follower. Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries PrevLogEntry check); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 with the post-restore block at raft.go:1930-1948 is the producer that must establish that condition.
basis.responsibility: Follower snapshot installation establishing a post-install last-log state compatible with the leader's AppendEntries and nextIndex catch-up loop.

comparisons.description: Control: isolated node's last index below the snapshot index still catches up to the leader commit index.
Case: with the isolated node's last index above the snapshot index, its applied index does not change across a 3s sample while the leader commit index is above it.
Case: the isolated node is still short of the leader commit index after the observation window.

experiments.revision_reason: Adds a third scenario using MakeClusterCustom with MonotonicLogs=true so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch, plus a store_monotonic field and a corresponding comparison. The control and the non-monotonic stall scenario are unchanged. This isolates whether the stall is caused by retained above-snapshot log bytes or by the cached last-log index/term.

result.summary:
Resuming the one registered necessary gap: does the catch-up stall persist for a MonotonicLogStore, where installSnapshot already deletes the above-snapshot bytes via removeOldLogs? The previous attempt exited 1 not on a target assertion but in the upstream test helper's own 5s shutdown timer (`cluster.Close()`, testing.go:307) after the snapshot-resend storm slowed teardown.

Fix (harness only, previous_id set with revision reason): `MakeClusterOpts.LongstopTimeout` raised from the helper default 5s to 60s, and each scenario now prints its `scenario_setup`/`snapshot_catchup_result` CA_EVENT pair inside the scenario function, before the deferred `cluster.Close()` runs, so a slow teardown cannot hide a completed measurement. Scenarios, prefix, requirement, anchors and comparisons are unchanged (control; non-monotonic stall; monotonic stall), with applicability `stale_suffix`/`store_monotonic` selecting the case and the assertion `stalled == false`.

Local native feedback (not the formal receipt): all three scenarios now emit and the run exits 0 — control holds (applied 55 = leader commit 55), non-monotonic stalls (applied 45, leader commit 55, stalled=true), and the monotonic case stalls identically (snapshot_index=45, old_last_before=223, old_last_after=223, applied 45, stalled=true) even though `removeOldLogs` emptied the store. That is the discriminator: the cause is the cached `lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm` that `installSnapshot` never resets (no `setLastLog`), read by `getLastEntry` (state.go:167-174) and rejected at the `PrevLogEntry` check (raft.go:1475-1502) — not the retained log bytes.

Envelope validates (`valid: true`). If the retained execution completes with exit 0, the monotonic gap can be answered and the predecessor's `unresolved` interpretation superseded; the primary defect conclusion from receipt 2322bd7884b749f89c3101f04bc82e78 is unchanged. Draft file: `draft/snapshot_suffix_monotonic_fix.json` (harness: `draft/snapshot_suffix_harness_monotonic.go`).

Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries PrevLogEntry check); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 with the post-restore block at raft.go:1930-1948 is the producer that must establish that condition.
requirement.after: After a follower installs a snapshot at index S, a persisted log suffix above S that the leader does not share must not keep the follower from accepting the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=S: the follower must stop reporting a stale above-snapshot last entry and converge to the leader's log. Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry returns the cached log index/term whenever it is at or above the snapshot index) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries rejects on a missing or term-mismatched PrevLogEntry); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 with the post-restore block at raft.go:1930-1948 is the producer responsible for establishing that state.

before.description: Control: isolated node's last index below the snapshot index still catches up to the leader commit index.
Case: with the isolated node's last index above the snapshot index, its applied index does not change across a 3s sample while the leader commit index is above it.
Case: the isolated node is still short of the leader commit index after the observation window.

after.description: Control (follower log at or below the snapshot index): the follower reaches the leader's commit index after snapshot catch-up.
Case (follower log extends above the snapshot index): the follower must also reach the leader's commit index; the retained run shows it does not.
Case: the follower's applied index must change across the observation window while the leader commit index is above it; the retained run shows it is frozen.

experiments.revision_reason: Corrected event and comparison encoding: the predecessor's comparisons required two mutually exclusive scenario_setup prerequisites to correlate to each result event, so all comparisons evaluated unknown. The successor emits one shared scenario_setup admission event and one shared snapshot_catchup_result event name per scenario, selects the scenario by a stale_suffix applicability condition, and asserts the required healthy property (isolated_caught_up true, stalled false) so a stalled case is a violating witness. The executed scenarios, prefix, requirement and observations are unchanged.

scope.description: One process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with FileSnapshotStore; each scenario selects InmemStore either directly (non-monotonic) or wrapped in MockMonotonicLogStore (monotonic) via MakeClusterCustom. The replacement leader compacts at or below its snapshot index (TrailingLogs=0).
assumptions: Config: ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, CommitTimeout=10ms, TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold disabled, SnapshotInterval=1h.
The isolated node's above-snapshot suffix is produced by real uncommitted Apply calls on the old leader before it steps down; no state is injected.
MockMonotonicLogStore returns IsMonotonic()==true, so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch.
excluded: Network and TCP transports; mixed-version rolling upgrades.
Restart or recovery of the isolated node; only live catch-up is measured.
Disk-backed stores (the in-memory stores share the same LogStore contract).

basis.prefix: For each of three scenarios: bootstrap a 3-node cluster, commit a 20-command prefix, isolate the current leader, append 2 (control) or 200 (both stall cases) uncommitted tail commands on the isolated node, let the remaining two nodes elect a replacement leader, commit 20 more commands and take a snapshot at index S, commit 10 post entries above S, reconnect, and observe for about 4.5s. The two stall scenarios differ only in the isolated node's log store (non-monotonic vs MockMonotonicLogStore).
basis.requirement: After a follower installs a snapshot at index S, catch-up must not depend on whether the above-S bytes survive: regardless of the LogStore's monotonicity, a follower whose persisted log ended above S must stop reporting a last log entry above S and accept the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=S so it converges to the leader's log. Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries PrevLogEntry check); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 chooses removeOldLogs for a MonotonicLogStore and compactLogs otherwise, and is the producer responsible for the post-install last-log state.
basis.responsibility: Follower snapshot installation establishing a post-install last-log state compatible with the leader's AppendEntries and nextIndex catch-up loop, for both monoticity branches of the LogStore.

comparisons.description: Control: isolated log at or below the snapshot index reaches the leader commit index.
Non-monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix must still catch up; the retained run shows it stalls.
Monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix: removeOldLogs deletes the bytes, yet the cached last-log state must not block catch-up; the retained run shows it still stalls.
